data.title: Out-of-Hours Contractor Access Unsupervised
data.summary: Cleaning, maintenance and security contractors held unescorted access to the whole building outside working hours, with vetting and key control managed by the contractor rather than by the organisation.
data.description:
Out-of-hours contractors have the access an intruder wants: every floor, every office, no observers, for hours. The access is legitimate, so it generates no alert.

Control of it is usually delegated. The organisation contracts a company, and that company decides who attends, with what vetting, and with what turnover. Individual attendees are often unknown to the client, change frequently, and are among the lowest-paid people with access to the building — which also makes them a target for recruitment or coercion.

Shared keys and codes compound it: a single alarm code and master key, known to everyone who has ever worked the contract.
data.recommendation:
* Vet contractor staff to the standard their access warrants, and require notification of changes.
* Issue individual credentials rather than shared keys and codes, and revoke them when an individual leaves the contract.
* Restrict out-of-hours access to the areas the work requires, excluding technical rooms and executive offices.
* Log and review out-of-hours access, and consider supervision or camera coverage for sensitive areas.
data.short_recommendation: Vet, badge and supervise out-of-hours access as you would staff.
